policy.townstead.clean_hearths.desc: Smoke hoods on every forge: workshops pollute half as much and catch fire less. Costs a little per workshop job.
policy.townstead.quiet_nights.desc: Shops and workshops close early: 40% less noise from them, but shops pay 10% less tax.
policy.townstead.market_days.desc: Weekly markets: shops always have customers and the town wants more of them, but they're louder.
policy.townstead.lantern_streets.desc: Lanterns along every road: land value +6. Costs a little per block of road.
policy.townstead.garden_town.desc: Window boxes and hanging baskets: homes +3 happiness, land value +3. Costs a little per household.
policy.townstead.old_town.desc: Keep the old charm: nothing grows past level 2, but land value +8 and homes +3 happiness.
policy.townstead.craft_relief.desc: Workshops pay half tax, and the town wants more of them.
policy.townstead.evening_classes.desc: Lessons after work: every home counts as having a school in reach. Costs a little per adult.
policy.townstead.free_coaches.desc: No fares: 40% more of the commuters near a line ride it. Town-wide only.
specialization.townstead.farming.desc: Industry grows as farms: fields, a barn and a granary. Almost no pollution, many unskilled jobs.
specialization.townstead.forestry.desc: Industry grows as lumber yards: log stacks, a saw shed and saplings. Some pollution, steady jobs; fires start more easily.
specialization.townstead.leisure.desc: Shops grow as taverns and inns: louder, but they pay 30% more tax.

advisor.townstead.roads.title: Lay your first road
advisor.townstead.roads: Everything in town grows along roads. Pick the Roads tool (second button), press 2 for a street, then click where it starts and where it ends.
advisor.townstead.zone_homes.title: Zone some homes
advisor.townstead.zone_homes: Pick the Zoning tool (third button), press 1 for homes and drag along your road. Settlers build houses on the lots, block by block.
advisor.townstead.utilities.title: Power and water
advisor.townstead.utilities: Homes need power and water to grow past level 1. Utilities tool (fourth button): 1 places a Windmill, 2 a Well. Put them beside a road: they reach every building along the connected roads.
advisor.townstead.jobs.title: Give people work
advisor.townstead.jobs: Residents need jobs and shops. Zone shops (3) along busy roads and industry (5) a little away from homes, since workshops are noisy and smoky. The RCIO bars at the top show what the town wants most.
advisor.townstead.more_utilities.title: Not enough power or water
advisor.townstead.more_utilities: %s buildings have no power and %s no water: your mills and wells are at capacity, or those buildings are on a road network without them. Build more, or join the roads up.
advisor.townstead.waiting.title: Building sites are waiting
advisor.townstead.waiting: %s sites have stopped for materials. The town's industry makes them over time; drop blocks into the Town Storehouse or buy them in (L, Production) to carry on now.
advisor.townstead.money.title: You're losing money
advisor.townstead.money: The town spends more each day than it earns. Press L for the budget: raise a tax by a point or two, or turn down a service you have plenty of. A small loan can bridge a gap.
advisor.townstead.unhappy.title: Unhappy residents
advisor.townstead.unhappy: %s buildings are unhappy and may be abandoned. With the Inspect tool, click one to see its happiness factors: often it's a missing service, noise, pollution or a long commute.
advisor.townstead.traffic.title: Traffic is jammed
advisor.townstead.traffic: Traffic flow is down to %s%%. Open the Info tool and press 8: red roads are over capacity. Widen them (lane to street, street to avenue), add a second route, or run a coach line along them.
advisor.townstead.service.title: Homes want a %s
advisor.townstead.service: %2$s homes have no %1$s in reach. Services make people happier and let buildings level up. Place one in the middle of them (Services or Parks tool); its ring shows what it covers.
advisor.townstead.demand.title: Your town wants %s
advisor.townstead.demand: Demand for %s is high. Zone more lots of that kind beside your roads and it will grow.
advisor.townstead.milestone.title: Next: %s
advisor.townstead.milestone: At %2$s people the town becomes %1$s: more emeralds, more land to buy and new buildings. Press U to see what each milestone unlocks.
advisor.townstead.good_town.title: How to build a good town
advisor.townstead.good_town: Press H twice in the planner for a short guide: keep homes away from industry, cover every home with services, keep the books positive and the roads flowing.

tool.townstead.zoning.desc: Paint lots for homes, shops, industry and offices; settlers build on them.
tool.townstead.utilities.desc: Windmills and watermills for power, wells and water towers for water.
tool.townstead.services.desc: Clinic, school, fire station, guard house and compost yard: each covers the homes in its ring.
tool.townstead.transport.desc: A Coach House and coach lines: riders leave the roads, and the town earns fares.
tool.townstead.parks.desc: Parks raise land value and make the homes around them happier.
tool.townstead.landmarks.desc: Unique buildings unlocked by milestones, with a big pull on happiness and land value.
tool.townstead.land.desc: Buy the land tiles around your town to grow into.
tool.townstead.info.desc: Overlays: power, water, services, happiness, land value, pollution, noise, education, traffic.

guide.townstead.title: How to build a good town
guide.townstead.1: 1. Start small: a street, a few homes, a windmill and a well. Grow outward as demand asks.
guide.townstead.2: 2. Watch the RCIO bars: zone what the town wants (Homes, Shops, Industry, Offices).
guide.townstead.3: 3. Keep industry apart from homes: its smoke and noise make neighbours unhappy. Shops and parks between them make a good buffer.
guide.townstead.4: 4. Power and water travel along roads: keep the network joined up and build more as the town grows (Info, keys 1-2).
guide.townstead.5: 5. Every home should be inside the ring of a clinic, a school, a fire station and a guard house. Parks and landmarks add happiness.
guide.townstead.6: 6. Buildings level up when they're happy and served; level 2 and up need power and water, or they're abandoned.
guide.townstead.7: 7. Keep the daily balance positive (L). Taxes around 9% are neutral; raise them a little when the town is happy.
guide.townstead.8: 8. Give roads room: avenues for main routes, streets for neighbourhoods, lanes only for quiet corners. Check traffic with Info, 8.
guide.townstead.9: 9. Coach lines take commuters off busy roads: stops near homes and near jobs on the same line.
guide.townstead.10: 10. Fire stations stop fires spreading; without one, a fire can burn a house down.
guide.townstead.11: 11. Use districts for character: Farming, Forestry or Quarry industry, Leisure shops, and policies like Garden Town for homes.
guide.townstead.12: 12. Industry feeds construction: farms, lumber yards and quarries make raw materials, workshops work them up. Check L, Production.
guide.townstead.more: Milestones (U) bring emeralds, land and new buildings. H again to close.
specialization.townstead.quarry.desc: Industry grows as quarries: terraced pits, a crane and a stone-cutting shed. They cut cobblestone (sandstone in the desert, terracotta in the savanna) and earth; dusty and loud like heavy industry.
